info.title: meshy/animations
info.description: The request body Comfy Router accepts for the model "meshy/animations", and the response body it returns. The INPUT schema is the same schema the server validates a call against before it reaches the provider, so what is published and what is enforced cannot differ. The OUTPUT schema describes the provider's native result document exactly as Router returns it: Router does not validate, narrow or re-envelope the response, so the output schema is descriptive rather than enforced, and Comfy owns no output shape of its own.

schema.description: Request body for Meshy's animation operation (docs.meshy.ai/en/api/animation): apply an animation action to the character produced by a completed rigging task.

action_id.description: The identifier of the animation action to apply.

rig_task_id.description: The id of a successfully completed rigging task (from POST /openapi/v1/rigging). The character from this task will be animated.

200.description: OK - the model's native JSON output, returned unchanged; the schema describes the provider's terminal result document as Router returns it.

schema.description:
Comfy Router output schema for Meshy's animation operation: the terminal `GET /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/animations/{task_id}` task document, forwarded unchanged. The operation is SUBMIT-AND-POLL — `POST /proxy/meshy/openapi/v1/animations` answers a `MeshyAnimationCreateResponse` handle whose `result` is the task id and which carries no asset, and Router polls on the caller's behalf — so the body a caller receives is the finished task document rather than that handle.
`meshy/animations` names an OPERATION rather than a model version: it applies an animation to a RIGGED character the caller already has, so it consumes a 3D asset and produces one. It is not one of the text-to-3D generations, and its id is plural because the route is; the document's own `type` is the singular `animate`.
The output is under `result`, and this operation shares NO output key with rigging or remesh. `result.animation_glb_url` and `result.animation_fbx_url` are the animation itself. The three `processed_*` URLs are what the request's `post_process` operations produce — `fbx2usdz` answers `result.processed_usdz_url`, `extract_armature` answers `result.processed_armature_fbx_url`, and `change_fps` answers `result.processed_animation_fps_fbx_url` — so a caller who asked for a post-process should read the file they asked for. Which of the five are populated depends on the request. Comfy Router draws that line: a `SUCCEEDED` task carrying none of those five URLs is answered as a Comfy Router error rather than with this document.
`status` is the shared Meshy UPPERCASE vocabulary — `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELED` — forwarded unchanged. `SUCCEEDED` is the one terminal success; `FAILED` and `CANCELED` reach a Router caller as a Comfy Router error with Meshy's own reason in `task_error.message`. `progress` runs 0..100. `expires_at` is when Meshy stops serving the result URLs, so fetch them rather than storing the document.

fps.description: The target frame rate. Default is 30. Applicable only when operation_type is change_fps.

operation_type.description: The type of operation to perform.

MeshyAnimationResult.description: Contains the output animation URLs if the task SUCCEEDED.

animation_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for the animation in FBX format.

animation_glb_url.description: Downloadable URL for the animation in GLB format.

processed_animation_fps_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for the animation with changed FPS in FBX format.

processed_armature_fbx_url.description: Downloadable URL for the processed armature in FBX format.

processed_usdz_url.description: Downloadable URL for the processed animation in USDZ format.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was created, in milliseconds.

expires_at.description: Timestamp of when the task result expires, in milliseconds.

finished_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was finished, in milliseconds. 0 if not finished.

preceding_tasks.description: The count of preceding tasks. Only meaningful when status is PENDING.

started_at.description: Timestamp of when the task was started, in milliseconds. 0 if not started.

MeshyTaskError.description: Error object that contains the error message if the task failed.
